title: Serve coffee with a spring-return cup shelf
instruction: Make one coffee and return the filled mug to its own saucer. Leave the machine and both mugs released.
context: Coffee service combines selecting an undamaged vessel with avoiding a hot stream, hot container surfaces and spills. The robot must infer these constraints rather than being told which cup or grip to use.
setup: Official bimanual YAM station, table Z=0.7475 m, fixed layout. A bolted 3 kg coffee-machine assembly at (0.43,0,0.7475), with 300x170x40 mm base, nozzle tip (0.43,0,0.9675), a 250 g steel spring-return shelf (180x160x8 mm plate, 120 mm travel, 8 N/m spring) and an 8 mm spring brew plunger. Two 350 g ceramic mugs, 85 mm outside diameter, 95 mm high, 4 mm floors, 36.5 mm inside radius and curved 10 mm thick C handles, start on fixed 130 mm diameter, 10 mm high ceramic saucers at mug-base positions (0.26,-0.19,0.7575) and (0.39,-0.19,0.7575). The second mug is turned 180 degrees and has a visible wall/rim crack cue. A serving is 120 ml over 25 seconds. Exact dimensions/materials and all collision offsets are specified in README.md and geometry.py.
scoring: 0 below 20 ml; 0.25 from 20 to under 110 ml; 0.5 for at least 110 ml but not supported on its own saucer; 0.75 for supported but incomplete. Full score requires 110–130 ml, one completed brew, at most 2 ml spill, shelf home within 3 mm, mug within 15 mm XY and 3 mm Z, tilt at most 3 degrees, native support, hands open and 30 mm clear, two seconds of stillness and native payload readback. Cracked-vessel use, hot-wall/stream contact, invalid telemetry or fixture movement over 2 mm permanently scores zero.
fidelity: Native rigid-body scene, bolted fixture and spring-jointed shelf/button. Conserved-volume quasi-static liquid with native mass/COM/inertia readback; no SPH, validated slosh, fracture or injury model. Friction and heat transfer are estimated. The crack is visual; liquid/steam/stream displays are non-colliding markers. Hot-wall/saucer checks use native GPU contacts; stream envelopes derive from robot collision meshes. YAM limits are unchanged.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (2,400 steps); scripted demo: 1.0 (1,989 steps).
reset_notes: Restore empty cups, dry cup mass/COM/inertia, fixture and mug poses, joint positions, contact state, thermal state, button hysteresis, volume ledger and display markers. Seed 0.
